note: SPECIMEN mlx_lm baseline+routing on a short prompt set; teacher=abliterated checkpoint. Route stats from ~10 prompts -> indicative, not full corpus.

CLASSIFICATION.uniform_routing: A3B-SPECIFIC / MOE-SPECIFIC -- entropy 6.09/7.00, no cold experts -> cold-expert compression (S042 §10) does NOT apply to A3B; per-expert uniform codec is fine, no popularity skew to exploit.
CLASSIFICATION.sparse_active_path: MOE-UNIVERSAL -- 8/128 experts/token ~= 3.6GB active-expert bytes/token vs dense 11.7GB (3.2x less). The lever is a native EXPERT-GATHER that MOVES only active experts, not all 128. mlx does not exploit it (29.3 TPS ~= dense).
CLASSIFICATION.tps_caveat: 29.3 is the mlx SPECIMEN; whether the 3.2x active-byte reduction becomes TPS depends on our runtime (Qwen3.8 finding: we are kernel-bound, not bandwidth-bound -- so a native MoE kernel must be efficient, not just move fewer bytes).
